correctness.rationale: Every derivation D(v+az)=Av+(φ(v)+ac)z obeys A²=A, c²=c, φA+cφ=φ, A†=cI-A. For c=0, A†=-A and A²=A imply 2A=0. Outside characteristic two this leaves zero; in characteristic two, self-adjoint idempotent A has orthogonal nondegenerate symplectic image/ker, so dim im(A)=2r. φ|ker A=0 and the full D rank is 2r. For c=1, im and ker of A are complementary Lagrangians of dimension m and φ|im A=0, so rank D=m+1. Central shears eliminate φ, symplectic automorphisms make each allowed projection class transitive, and c and r separate orbits. Counting nondegenerate 2r-subspaces by |Sp(2m,q)|/[|Sp(2r,q)||Sp(2m-2r,q)|], transversely paired Lagrangians by ∏(q^i+1)q^{m(m+1)/2}, and φ choices q^{2r},q^m yields the stated rank polynomial. Independent matrix enumeration confirmed H_1(F2)={0:1,2:16}, H_1(F3)={0:1,2:36}, H_2(F2)={0:1,2:80,3:480,4:16}. Finite tests corroborate but do not prove all fields/dimensions.
residual_risks: The count of transverse Lagrangian complements as graphs of symmetric bilinear maps must be interpreted correctly also in characteristic two; the source proof does so.
All-field normal-form transitivity relies on standard symplectic basis extension.

value.rationale: The Heisenberg family is the central model of nonabelian two-step nilpotent Lie algebras. The theorem resolves exact conjugacy and labeled idempotent-operator ranks for every field, with a genuine characteristic-two phase change from two to m+2 orbits. Both the orbit census and finite-q polynomial provide structural data not contained in the general derivation presentation; small m=2,q=2 already shows three nonzero full ranks 2,3,4.
residual_risks: Uses classical symplectic linear algebra as principal technology; no unsupported wider classification of all two-step algebras is claimed.

final_claim: For every field K and standard (2m+1)-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra H_m(K), ordinary composition-idempotent derivations have two conjugacy classes if char K!=2 and m+2 if char K=2; the c=0 branches have ranks 2r and the c=1 branch rank m+1, with the complete finite-field labeled rank polynomial P_{m,q}(X) displayed in frozen RESULT.md.
limitations: Standard Heisenberg Lie algebra over an arbitrary field only; full rank polynomial over finite fields.
Finite matrix counts do not certify unrestricted m or field characteristic.
